# Thesis: NEAR Intents volume as a leading indicator of NEAR network usage

Generated by `npm run rebuild` (`scripts/thesis.ts`) from the committed raw files on {{asOf}}. Every number below is recomputed from `data/history` and `data/raw`; nothing is typed in by hand. The same numbers drive the `/thesis` page.

## Claim

Cross-chain volume settled through NEAR Intents is a better leading indicator of real NEAR network usage than the NEAR token price. "Leading" means: changes in Intents volume this week are more strongly correlated with changes in usage one or more weeks later than changes in price are, and a model fitted on earlier data predicts later usage changes better when it uses Intents volume than when it uses price.

## Data and method

- Window: {{windowStart}} to {{windowEnd}} ({{weeks}} ISO weeks). Intents volume comes from DefiLlama's NEAR Intents adapter (all channels, daily, since 2024-12-10). Usage comes from the NEAR BigQuery public dataset (transactions and active accounts over the whole window; function calls and distinct contracts called over the last {{bqWeeks}} weeks, {{bqStart}} to {{bqEnd}}) and from NearBlocks daily charts (new accounts), series by series as in the table below. Price is NearBlocks' daily NEAR price (DefiLlama coins as a cross-check).
- All series are resampled to ISO weeks (flows summed, price and account counts as weekly totals or last values), converted to week-over-week log changes, and compared at lags of −{{maxLag}} to +{{maxLag}} weeks. A positive lag means the predictor moves first.
- Out-of-sample: a one-variable regression of usage change on the lagged predictor change is fitted on weeks before {{cutoff}} (lag picked on the training window only) and scored on weeks from {{cutoff}} onward with out-of-sample R² (against the training mean) and the share of weeks where the predicted sign was right.
- Robustness: the same tests with the largest 5% of Intents volume days capped, and again with those days removed, with receipts to `aurora` and `intents.near` removed from function calls, on daily instead of weekly data, and with the 1Click Explorer volume in place of DefiLlama's where the Explorer backfill covers it.

## How to reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/wazarat/near-dashboard.git && cd near-dashboard
npm ci
npm run rebuild      # recomputes every chart, table and this file from the committed raw data; no network, no secrets
npm run build        # static site in out/ (the /thesis page shows the same numbers with the SQL and API calls behind each chart)
```

To refresh the raw data instead: `npm run refresh` (DefiLlama, NearBlocks and NEAR Catalog need no keys; BigQuery needs `GCP_PROJECT_ID` with Application Default Credentials; the Intents Explorer needs `NEAR_INTENTS_JWT`). Sources: `queries/daily_chain.sql`, `queries/daily_receipts.sql`, `https://api.llama.fi/overview/dexs/near`, `https://api.nearblocks.io/v1/charts`, `https://explorer.near-intents.org/api/v0/transactions`.

### Verify the evidence

Each daily refresh writes two SHA-256 fingerprints to NEAR mainnet through SocialDB (`canhav.near/canhav-atlas/anchors/<date>`): one over every committed raw file the rebuild reads, one over what `npm run rebuild` writes. The transaction for each date is listed in `data/anchors/index.json` and the per-file hashes in `data/anchors/<date>.manifest.txt`.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/wazarat/near-dashboard.git && cd near-dashboard && git checkout <commit>
npm ci
npm run verify:anchor -- <date> --rebuild
```

A match on both fingerprints proves the evidence existed on that date and that the published numbers are rebuilt from it unchanged.
